title: Frame
blurb: I ran a topology study on the frame model to see where the material was doing no work. The inner faces of the central hexagon are fixed, and a 7 N upward force is applied at the mounting holes for the arm blocks, 2 holes per block and 4 per arm. The target was about 30% less mass.

It said geometry close to the center could be thinned and geometry near the perimeter could be removed. I then ran a static study on the optimized frame with the same fixtures and force: removing the perimeter geometry has little impact on strength or deflection.

title: Arms and propulsion
blurb: I sized the arm as a cantilever tube: 16 lbf at the tip, 14.99 in out from the frame. The purchased carbon tube is 0.996 in OD by 0.875 in ID. Bending stress is 6115 psi against the 500,000 psi tensile strength I used, the tip deflects 0.033 in, and the tube weighs 0.160 lb.
Twist gets its own check: 1.11 N·m over 0.35 m turns the tube 0.0012 rad, about 0.07°.

Six arms instead of four because hover thrust divides by motor count. At the same weight a hexacopter motor hovers at about 33% of its maximum thrust where a quad motor needs about 49%, and six motors means it can lose one and still fly to some extent. The cost is power draw: a hexacopter flies about 15 minutes at max throttle.
note: The thrust split and the 15 minute flight time are estimates from the published sources in my hexacopter configuration research, not measurements from this airframe.

title: Battery
blurb: The pack is a TATTU 22 Ah, held by two 25 mm velcro straps on a printed TPU mount.

title: Electronics
blurb: The avionics are real vendor parts: a Pixhawk 6X with its baseboard, and an RTK GPS. I contributed to the mounts they sit on (the Pixhawk mount plate, the RTK mount and the shunt plug mount) and modeled or imported the vendor parts next to them.

title: Landing gear
blurb: Folding landing gear on three legs. Each leg is a CF-Kevlar tube with a top plate, four support struts, a support ring and a TPU foot.

title: Payload
blurb: A servo-actuated payload-drop mechanism: an MG90S servo and horn, an indented servo attachment, a top fixed plate and a TPU slotted housing. The drone is a platform, so a number of different payloads can be attached to it, which is why the payload mount is a subassembly of its own.
